title: The lead story
content: The UAE is revising the blueprint for its planned 5-gigawatt AI data-center campus after the Iran war exposed new physical-security risks.

title: From one campus to a network
content: Reuters reports the project will likely shift from one 10-square-mile Abu Dhabi campus toward a network of data centers across the UAE.

title: Resilience is driving the redesign
content: The reported changes aim to reduce vulnerability to drone and missile attacks while keeping the AI-infrastructure programme moving.

title: Underground construction is on the table
content: Officials are considering placing some infrastructure underground as part of the hardening effort, according to Reuters sources.

title: Air defence enters data-center design
content: The redesign is reported to include drone and missile interceptors plus electronic jamming.

title: The first phase is still moving
content: The initial 1-gigawatt Stargate UAE phase is expected to continue with protective modifications rather than a wholesale stop.

title: The first 200 MW remains the near-term milestone
content: The first 200 megawatts had been scheduled for 2026; today’s reporting does not say that milestone has been cancelled.

title: The partner stack is unusually broad
content: The programme connects G42 with OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, Cisco and SoftBank, with U.S. government involvement in the wider framework.

title: Recent attacks changed the threat model
content: Reuters says two AWS data centers in the UAE and one in Bahrain were damaged in Iranian attacks in March.

title: G42 says the project remains on track
content: G42 told Reuters work is progressing as planned while project specifics remain under continuous security and resilience review.

title: The original campus target is 5 GW
content: The wider UAE–U.S. AI Campus was announced with a target of 5 gigawatts of AI data-center capacity.

title: The original footprint is 10 square miles
content: G42 described the original campus as spanning about 10 square miles, roughly 26 square kilometres.

title: Stargate UAE is a 1 GW cluster
content: Within the larger campus, Stargate UAE is a separate 1-gigawatt compute cluster.

title: Reuters values phase one at $30 billion
content: Reuters describes the first 1-gigawatt Stargate UAE phase as a $30-billion compute cluster.

title: 200 MW was planned for 2026
content: OpenAI and G42 both said the first 200-megawatt cluster was expected to go live in 2026.

title: G42 is building Stargate UAE
content: G42 is the principal UAE technology group leading construction of the Stargate UAE cluster.

title: OpenAI and Oracle are operators
content: G42’s original announcement said OpenAI and Oracle would operate the 1-gigawatt Stargate UAE cluster.

title: Nvidia is part of the compute plan
content: G42 said Nvidia would supply Grace Blackwell GB300 systems for Stargate UAE.

title: Cisco is part of the infrastructure layer
content: Cisco was announced as a partner providing zero-trust security and AI-ready connectivity.

title: SoftBank is another Stargate partner
content: SoftBank is part of the consortium around Stargate UAE alongside OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, Cisco and G42.

title: The original power plan mixes sources
content: G42’s original campus announcement said the 5GW facility would be powered by nuclear, solar and natural gas.

title: It is OpenAI’s first international Stargate
content: OpenAI introduced Stargate UAE in 2025 as the first international deployment of its Stargate infrastructure programme.

title: It launched with OpenAI for Countries
content: OpenAI also described Stargate UAE as the first partnership under its OpenAI for Countries initiative.

title: The project has a cross-border investment component
content: The bilateral plan pairs UAE compute construction with UAE investment into U.S. Stargate infrastructure.

title: The programme sits inside a U.S.–UAE security framework
content: The wider AI partnership includes U.S. technology access, investment commitments and security conditions around advanced infrastructure.

title: Why the UAE wants frontier compute
content: The UAE has used AI and digital infrastructure as part of a broader strategy to diversify its economy beyond hydrocarbons.

title: Compute has become strategic infrastructure
content: Frontier AI depends on chips, networking, electricity, cooling and secure data-center capacity, making compute a national-strategy issue.

title: The campus was announced in 2025
content: The UAE–U.S. AI Campus was unveiled during President Donald Trump’s UAE visit in May 2025.

title: The bilateral framework matters
content: The U.S.–UAE AI Acceleration Partnership is the political framework supporting the campus and related technology cooperation.

title: Sovereign AI is part of the pitch
content: The campus is intended to give the UAE and region access to large-scale AI compute under a trusted bilateral framework.

title: AI campuses concentrate enormous power demand
content: A 5GW design makes energy architecture inseparable from compute architecture.

title: Mega-campuses offer efficiency
content: A single large campus can simplify fibre, power delivery, cooling, construction logistics and operations.

title: Mega-campuses also concentrate risk
content: Putting very large amounts of compute in one location creates a physical single point of failure during war or infrastructure outages.

title: Distribution trades efficiency for resilience
content: Spreading capacity across several sites can reduce correlated failure risk but adds networking, replication and operating complexity.

title: Underground data centers already exist
content: Reuters notes that data centers have been built in mines, bunkers and caves in the United States, China and Europe.

title: Mountains can provide natural protection
content: Reuters says officials have considered mountain locations for facilities holding the most sensitive data, including military data.

title: The UAE has suitable mountain regions
content: Mountain ranges in Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah differ from the UAE’s predominantly flat desert terrain.

title: Al Dhafra is strategically sensitive
content: Reuters reports the original campus site is near Al Dhafra Air Base, which hosts U.S. troops and has been targeted during the war.

title: Cloud outages make resilience visible
content: Damage to regional data centers demonstrated that digital services can be disrupted by physical attacks.

title: This is infrastructure planning under wartime assumptions
content: The reported redesign moves AI campus planning beyond cost, power and cooling toward defence, continuity and survivability.

title: UAE government
content: The UAE is the host state, policy sponsor and national beneficiary of the wider AI-infrastructure programme.

title: G42
content: G42 leads the UAE side of the campus and is central to both construction and the country’s wider AI strategy.

title: Sheikh Tahnoun bin Zayed
content: Reuters identifies G42 as controlled by Sheikh Tahnoun bin Zayed al Nahyan, the UAE national security adviser and brother of the president.

title: OpenAI
content: OpenAI is the anchor frontier-AI partner and says it is making progress with the UAE on infrastructure and adoption priorities.

title: Oracle
content: Oracle is an operating partner in Stargate UAE and part of the Stargate infrastructure consortium.

title: Nvidia
content: Nvidia supplies advanced AI accelerators that are essential to the cluster’s compute capability.

title: Cisco
content: Cisco provides connectivity and security infrastructure for the original Stargate UAE design.

title: SoftBank
content: SoftBank participates in the Stargate consortium and its financing-and-infrastructure ecosystem.

title: U.S. government
content: The United States is central because advanced chip exports, security conditions and investment commitments are part of the arrangement.

title: UAE advanced technology authorities
content: UAE technology authorities oversee advanced-technology policy, though Reuters said the ministry did not comment on the reported redesign.

title: Amazon Web Services
content: AWS is relevant because Reuters reports regional AWS facilities were damaged in the March attacks.

title: Iran
content: Iran is the military actor whose attacks and explicit warning about Stargate UAE changed the project’s physical threat environment.

title: Al Dhafra Air Base
content: The nearby base matters because its U.S. military role increases the strategic sensitivity of the surrounding area.

title: Regional enterprises and government agencies
content: Oracle has said the completed infrastructure could connect UAE public and commercial institutions to advanced AI models.

title: Regional AI users
content: OpenAI has framed Stargate UAE as infrastructure capable of serving users within roughly a 2,000-mile radius.

title: Threat modelling now includes kinetic attack
content: The design problem is no longer only cyber intrusion or component failure; it now includes missiles, drones and blast damage.

title: Site dispersion reduces correlated failure
content: Separating facilities geographically makes it harder for one strike or local outage to remove the entire compute estate.

title: Underground construction adds physical shielding
content: Buried facilities can reduce blast exposure but complicate excavation, ventilation, cooling and emergency access.

title: Blast-resistant concrete hardens the envelope
content: Reuters reports blast-resistant concrete is among the measures under consideration.

title: Interceptors create an active-defence layer
content: Drone and missile interceptors would add military-style active protection around critical AI infrastructure.

title: Electronic jamming targets guidance links
content: Electronic jamming can disrupt some drone communications or navigation, adding another defensive layer around fixed sites.

title: Backup power becomes more important
content: Reuters says additional backup power is being considered because attacks can disable grid connections even when servers survive.

title: Backup cooling is equally critical
content: AI accelerators generate intense heat, so compute can become unavailable quickly if cooling systems fail.

title: Distributed sites need stronger networking
content: A multi-site architecture requires high-capacity links so workloads, checkpoints and data can move between facilities.

title: Replication becomes a resilience tool
content: Critical data and services can be copied across sites so one damaged location does not become the only serving point.

title: Workload placement becomes strategic
content: Operators can place models or datasets at more exposed, hardened or remote locations based on sensitivity.

title: Latency is a trade-off
content: A distributed estate can increase inter-site latency, so architecture must balance resilience against performance.

title: Power planning becomes multi-regional
content: Several facilities require grid connections, substations, generation and backup capacity across multiple locations.

title: Chip security remains part of the system
content: Advanced accelerators are export-controlled strategic components, so physical resilience sits alongside supply-chain controls.

title: Resilience changes total cost
content: Hardening, underground works, redundant power and cooling, extra networking and multiple sites can all raise costs.

title: Implication: AI infrastructure is becoming defence infrastructure
content: The redesign suggests leading AI campuses may increasingly be treated like strategic assets needing military-grade continuity planning.

title: Implication: geography matters more than before
content: Site selection may increasingly weigh distance from military targets and natural protection alongside electricity and fibre.

title: Implication: hyperscale concentration may lose some appeal
content: Higher conflict risk can make distributed capacity worth the complexity that one giant campus avoids.

title: Implication: sovereign AI needs sovereign resilience
content: Countries seeking domestic AI capability must protect the physical facilities that keep models and data available.

title: Implication: cloud architecture and national security are converging
content: Redundancy, failover and distribution are being applied at the level of whole AI campuses.

title: Implication: insurers and lenders may reprice risk
content: Persistent regional threats could make hardening and geographic diversification more important to financing and insurance.

title: Implication: schedules could become harder to predict
content: Security redesign can affect engineering and sequencing, although Reuters could not determine the final timeline impact.

title: Implication: power redundancy becomes a premium feature
content: AI sites may need more on-site generation, storage and backup systems to survive grid damage or fuel disruption.

title: Implication: sensitive workloads may split from commercial workloads
content: Possible mountain facilities for military data point toward different physical tiers for different AI workloads.

title: Implication: U.S. partners inherit regional risk
content: American AI companies gain capacity and market reach but also exposure to regional physical-security risk.

title: Implication: advanced chips become harder to defend at scale
content: A 5GW AI estate concentrates scarce accelerators, increasing the value of physical protection and continuity planning.

title: Implication: security-technology demand could rise
content: Large AI campuses may become customers for counter-drone systems, hardened construction, monitoring and backup energy.

title: Implication: resilience may become an AI-campus benchmark
content: Future projects may be compared on recoverability and attack tolerance as well as megawatts, GPUs and cost.

title: Implication: the Gulf remains strategically important
content: Despite higher security concerns, the UAE still offers capital, energy, connectivity and state backing for frontier-scale AI.

title: Implication: the project is a test case
content: How Stargate UAE adapts may influence sovereign AI infrastructure design in other geopolitically exposed regions.

title: Watch: is a new masterplan formally announced?
content: A formal layout would clarify how radical the reported redesign becomes.

title: Watch: does total capacity stay at 5 GW?
content: The key question is whether geographic distribution changes only the layout or also the long-term capacity target.

title: Watch: does the first 200 MW arrive in 2026?
content: Any delay or confirmation of the original 200MW milestone will be the clearest short-run execution signal.

title: Watch: where are the additional sites?
content: Future announcements could reveal which emirates or regions host the distributed facilities.

title: Watch: which workloads go underground?
content: The split between conventional, underground and possible mountain sites will show how the threat model is operationalised.

title: Watch: how much does hardening cost?
content: Reuters could not determine the cost impact; revised capex would reveal the financial price of resilience.

title: Watch: do timelines change?
content: A distributed, hardened design may require new engineering, but no final schedule impact has been established.

title: Watch: what happens to the original Abu Dhabi site?
content: The first phase is expected to continue with modifications while later phases may disperse.

title: Watch: are air-defence systems dedicated to data centers?
content: Confirmed interceptors or jamming around civilian AI infrastructure would mark a significant protection shift.

title: Watch: do U.S. export rules change?
content: Advanced chip licensing remains central, so new U.S. security conditions could affect deployment pace or architecture.

title: Watch: how OpenAI and Oracle adjust operations
content: Multi-site compute may require new workload-placement, replication and failover practices.

title: Watch: whether regional cloud disruptions clear
content: Recovery of damaged Gulf cloud infrastructure will show how quickly data-center services can rebound from kinetic attacks.

title: Watch: whether other Gulf projects copy the model
content: Other regional investors may reassess concentration and hardening as they expand AI and cloud infrastructure.

title: Watch: whether resilience becomes a selling point
content: Future AI-campus announcements may advertise hardened design as explicitly as GPUs, megawatts and model access.

title: Watch the ScrollAI signal
content: Measure sessions, scroll depth and monetisation before scaling this infrastructure-and-security explainer beyond Top 100.
